Build a classic CrewAI-style starter project that students can extend into a working
research crew. Use Python 3.10-3.13, crewai[tools] 1.15.x, and the traditional
src-layout Python/YAML scaffold with declarative agent/task configuration separated from
orchestration.

Required structure:
- Define a senior researcher and a reporting analyst in agent configuration, including
  role, goal, and backstory fields.
- Define two sequential tasks: produce ten relevant bullet points for a topic and
  current year, then expand that context into a detailed Markdown report written to
  report.md.
- Keep the starter topic fixed to “AI LLMs” so the initial run path is obvious.
- Keep the runtime entry point thin and expose run, train, replay, and evaluation
  commands.
- Interpolate topic into agent and task configuration, and current_year into the
  research task. Run verbosely and surface failures with useful context.

Important teaching constraint: intentionally attach no web-search or research tool.
Include an obvious custom-tool stub, but leave it unused. The project should make the
limitation visible: without a real evidence tool, the researcher can only rely on model
knowledge and must not be presented as current web research.

Never commit real provider keys. Ignore local environment files and provide a safe
.env.example with model and credential placeholders. Do not commit generated report
files, caches, or virtual environments.

Highlight pitfalls: mismatched YAML variable names fail at runtime; configured methods
must match agent/task names; an unattached tool does nothing; “researcher” does not
imply web access; and live model output is nondeterministic and billable.

Add offline configuration/wiring tests and a mocked sequential-run smoke test. Include
concise runtime-version, dependency, environment, command, output, layout, test,
extension-point, and known-limitation documentation.
